source_text: Πόθεν δὲ τῷ Κέλσου Ἰουδαίῳ λέλεκται ὅτι ἐκρύπτετο Ἰησοῦς; λέγει γὰρ περὶ αὐτοῦ· τίς δὲ πώποτε πεμφθεὶς ἄγγελος, δέον ἀγγέλλειν τὰ κεκελευσμένα, κρύπτεται; οὐ γὰρ ἐκρύπτετο ὁ εἰπὼν τοῖς ζητοῦσιν αὐτὸν συλλαβεῖν· „καθ᾿ ἡμέραν ἤμην ἐν τῷ ἱερῷ ἱερῷ παῤῥησίᾳ διδάσκων, καὶ οὐκ ἐκρατήσατέ με,“ πρὸς δὲ τὸ ἑξῆς παλιλλογούμενον ὑπὸ τοῦ Κέλσου ἡμεῖς ἅπαξ ἀπολογησάμενοι ἀρκεσθησόμεθα τοῖς προειρημένοις. γέγραπται γὰρ ἐν τοῖς ἀνωτέρω καὶ πρὸς τὸ ἢ ὅτε μὲν ἠπιστεῖτο ἐν σώματι, πᾶσιν ἀνέδην ἐκήρυττεν· ὅτε δὲ πίστιν ἂν ἰσχυρὰν παρεῖχεν ἐκ νεκρῶν ἀναστὰς, ἑνὶ μόνῳ γυναίῳ καὶ τοῖς ἑαυτοῦ θιασώταις κρύβδην παρεφαίνετο; ἀλλ᾿ οὐδ᾿ ὅτι ἑνὶ μόνῳ γυναίῳ ἐφάνη, ἀληθές ἐστιν· γέγραπται γὰρ ἐν τῷ κατὰ Ματθαῖον εὐαγγελίῳ ὅτι „ὀψὲ σαββάτων. τῇ ἐπιφωσκούσῃ εἰς μίαν σαββάτων, ἦλθε Μαρία ἡ Μαγδαληνὴ καὶ ἡ ἄλλη Μαρία, θεωρῆσαι τὸν τάφον. καὶ ἰδοὺ σεισμὸς ἐγένετο μέγας· ἄγγελος γὰρ κυρίου καταβὰς ἐξ οὐρανοῦ καὶ προσελθὼν ἀπεκύλισε τὸν λίθον.“ καὶ μετ᾿ ὀλίγον φησὶν ὁ Ματθαῖος· „καὶ ἰδοὺ ὁ Ἰησοῦς ὑπήντησεν αὐταῖς“ (δῆλον δ᾿ ὅτι ταῖς προειρημέναις Μαρίαις) „λέγων· χαίρετε. αἱ δὲ προσελθοῦσαι ἐκράτησαν αὐτοῦ τοὺς πόδας καὶ προσεκύνησαν αὐτῷ.“ λέλεκται δὲ καὶ πρὸς τὸ κολαζόμενος μὲν ἄρα πᾶσιν ἑωρᾶτο, ἀναστὰς δὲ ἑνὶ, ὅτε ἀπελογούμεθα πρὸς τὸ οὐ πᾶσιν ἑωρᾶτο. καὶ νῦν δὲ φήσομεν ὅτι τὰ μὲν ἀνθρώπινα αὐτοῦ πᾶσιν ἦν ὁρατὰ. τὰ δὲ θειότερα (λέγω δὲ οὐ περὶ τῶν σχέσιν πρὸς ἕτερα ἐχόντων ἀλλὰ περὶ τῶν κατὰ διαφορὰν) οὐ πᾶσι χωρητά. πρόσχες δὲ καὶ τῇ παρὰ πόδας τοῦ Κέλσου ἐναντιότητι πρὸς ἑαυτόν. προειπὼν γοῦν ἑνὶ γυναίῳ καὶ τοῖς ἑαυτοῦ θιασώταις κρύβδην αὐτὸν παραπεφάνθαι εὐθέως ἐπιφέρει· κολαζόμενος μὲν ἄρα πᾶσιν ἑωρᾶτο, ἀναστὰς δὲ ἑνὶ, οὗπερ ἐχρῆν τοὐναντίον. τί δὲ καὶ νομίζει τὸ ἐχρῆν. ἀκούσωμεν. ἐναντίον τοῦ μὲν κολαζόμενον πᾶσιν ἑωρᾶσθαι, ἀναστάντα δὲ ἑνί· ὅσον γὰρ ἐπὶ τῇ λέξει ἑαυτοῦ ἤθελε καὶ ἀδύνατον καὶ ἄλογον, κολαζόμενον μὲν ἑνὶ ὁρᾶσθαι, ἀναστάντα δὲ πᾶσιν· ἢ πῶς διηγήσῃ τὸ οὗπερ ἐχρῆν τοὐναντίον;
pass_a_gloss: From where (πόθεν) has it been said (λέγω) by the Jew of Celsus (ὁ Κέλσου Ἰουδαῖος) that Jesus was hiding (κρύπτω, imperf. mid.)? For he says about him: 'Who ever, sent (πέμπω) as messenger (ἄγγελος), it being necessary (δέον) to announce (ἀγγέλλω) the things commanded (κελεύω), hides himself?' For he was not hiding who said to those seeking (ζητέω) to seize (συλλαμβάνω) him: 'Daily (καθ' ἡμέραν) I was in the temple (ἱερόν) teaching (διδάσκω) with boldness/openly (παρρησία), and you did not lay hold (κρατέω) of me.' Toward the next thing, repeated (παλιλλογέω) by Celsus, we, having answered (ἀπολογέομαι) once (ἅπαξ), will be content (ἀρκέω) with the things said before. For it has been written in the things above also toward this: 'Or, when he was disbelieved (ἀπιστέω) in body (σῶμα), he proclaimed (κηρύσσω) to all without restraint (ἀνέδην); but when he would have provided strong faith (πίστις ἰσχυρά) having risen (ἀνίστημι) from dead, to one only little woman (γύναιον, diminutive) and to his own fellow-cultists (θιασώτης, member of a θίασος) he appeared-alongside (παραφαίνομαι) secretly (κρύβδην)?' But not even that he appeared to one only little woman is true; for it is written in the according-to-Matthew gospel that 'late of sabbaths (ὀψὲ σαββάτων), at the dawning (ἐπιφώσκω) toward one (first day) of sabbaths, came Mary the Magdalene and the other Mary to view (θεωρέω) the tomb (τάφος). And behold a great earthquake (σεισμός) happened; for an angel of the Lord (ἄγγελος κυρίου), having come down from heaven and having approached, rolled away (ἀποκυλίω) the stone.' And after a little Matthew says: 'And behold Jesus met (ὑπαντάω) them' (clear that the aforesaid Marys) 'saying: Rejoice (χαίρετε). And they, having approached, grasped (κρατέω) his feet and did obeisance/worshiped (προσκυνέω) him.' It has been said also toward 'punished (κολάζω), then (ἄρα), he was seen by all, but having risen, by one,' when we were answering toward 'he was not seen by all.' And now we shall say that his human things (τὰ ἀνθρώπινα) were visible (ὁρατά) to all, but the more divine (θειότερα) (I speak not about those having relation (σχέσις) toward other things, but about those according to difference/differentia (κατὰ διαφοράν)) not to all receivable/containable (χωρητά). Attend also to the at-hand (παρὰ πόδας) contrariety (ἐναντιότης) of Celsus toward himself. Having said before that to one little woman and his own fellow-cultists secretly he appeared, straightway he adds: 'punished then he was seen by all, but having risen by one, of which the contrary (τοὐναντίον) was needed (χρή, ἐχρῆν).' And what he thinks the 'was needed' is, let us hear. Contrary to: punished being seen by all, risen by one; for so far as at his own wording (λέξις) he wanted a thing both impossible (ἀδύνατον) and irrational (ἄλογον): punished to be seen by one, risen by all. Or how will you narrate/explain (διηγέομαι) 'of which the contrary was needed'?
pass_b_english: On what grounds has Celsus’s Jew said that Jesus was in hiding? For he says of him: “Who, sent as a messenger, ever hides himself when he ought to announce what he has been commanded?” Yet the one who said to those seeking to arrest him, “Day after day I was in the temple, teaching openly, and you did not seize me” (Mark 14:49; compare Matthew 26:55; John 18:20), was not hiding.

As for the next point, which Celsus repeats, we have answered it once and will be content with what we said before. For above we have also written a reply to this: “Or did he, while he was disbelieved in the body, preach freely to all, but, when he could have produced strong faith by rising from the dead, show himself secretly to one little woman alone and to his own band of followers?”

But it is not even true that he appeared to one little woman alone. For it is written in the Gospel according to Matthew: “After the sabbath, as the first day of the week was dawning, Mary Magdalene and the other Mary came to see the tomb. And behold, there was a great earthquake; for an angel of the Lord came down from heaven, approached and rolled away the stone” (Matthew 28:1–2). And a little later Matthew says: “And behold, Jesus met them” (clearly, the Marys mentioned before), “saying, ‘Greetings.’ And they came up, took hold of his feet and worshiped him” (Matthew 28:9).

An answer has also been given to “So when he was being punished he was seen by all, but when he had risen, by one,” when we offered our defense on the point that he was not seen by all. And now too we will say that what was human in him was visible to all, but what was more divine in him (I mean not what consists in a relation to something else, but what is so by its own distinguishing character) was not open to all to receive.

Notice also how Celsus at once contradicts himself. Thus, having said just before that he appeared secretly to one little woman and to his own band of followers, he immediately adds: “So when he was being punished he was seen by all, but when he had risen, by one, whereas the opposite ought to have happened.” Let us hear what he thinks ought to have happened. It was the opposite of his being seen by all when punished and by one when risen; for, so far as his own wording goes, he wanted something both impossible and unreasonable: that when punished he should be seen by one, but when risen, by all. Or how will you explain “whereas the opposite ought to have happened”?

translator_notes: Celsus’s words are marked in double quotation marks as Origen frames them: the messenger question; the earlier objection Origen recalls (‘Or did he...’); ‘So when he was being punished... by one’; and the closing ‘whereas the opposite ought to have happened’ (οὗπερ ἐχρῆν τοὐναντίον). πρὸς τὸ οὐ πᾶσιν ἑωρᾶτο (‘on the point that he was not seen by all’) names the topic of Origen’s own earlier defense, so it is left unquoted rather than attributed to Celsus. Celsus plays on ἄγγελος/ἀγγέλλειν; rendered ‘messenger... announce’. The staged text reads ἐν τῷ ἱερῷ ἱερῷ, an obvious dittography; translated once. The temple saying is a conflation: ἤμην... ἐν τῷ ἱερῷ διδάσκων καὶ οὐκ ἐκρατήσατέ με matches Mark 14:49; καθ’ ἡμέραν and the setting match Matthew 26:55 (ἐκαθεζόμην); παρρησίᾳ comes from John 18:20; Luke 22:53 is a further parallel. Origen’s Matthew 28:1-2 lacks δέ after ὀψέ and has Μαρία for Μαριάμ; otherwise it agrees with the NT text. At Matthew 28:9 he has ὁ Ἰησοῦς with the article. ὀψὲ σαββάτων rendered ‘After the sabbath’ (it can also mean ‘late on the sabbath’). γύναιον is a diminutive, kept as ‘little woman’ because Celsus uses it to belittle. θιασῶται, members of a religious band, rendered ‘band of followers’. The parenthesis on ‘relation’ versus ‘differentia’ uses Stoic categories (πρός τί πως ἔχοντα versus κατὰ διαφοράν): Origen distinguishes what is said of Christ in relation to others from what he is by his own distinctive character; rendered by sense, without adding a subject. The ‘earlier’ answers point back to Origen’s replies earlier in Book 2 to the ‘one woman’ and ‘not seen by all’ objections; no chapter numbers added.
